The Data Co-ordinator manages data and systems for early careers and apprenticeship programs. Responsibilities include running the Learner Management System (LMS), tracking Individual Learner Records (ILRs) to secure government funding, and keeping records compliant with Ofsted and ESFA standards. - A good working knowledge of IT systems, including experience with data management tools and software like Learner Management Systems (LMS).
- The ability to take initiative, solve problems, and work independently as part of a virtual team.
- Good presentation skills to clearly share funding reports, data trends, and process updates with the team.

Desirable Requirements:
- Prior experience working with Education Skills Funding Agency (ESFA) rules, funding methodologies, or managing the Apprenticeship Levy pool.
- Direct experience preparing, validating, or submitting Individual Learner Records (ILRs) using data compliance tools.
- Familiarity with popular apprenticeship and learner management software systems (such as Maytas, Aptem, OneFile, or Tribal).
- Prior experience participating in or preparing documentation for Ofsted inspections or external funding audits in a training/further education environment.

title: Operational Administrator
description:
Operational Administrator

We are seeking a proactive, organised and commercially minded Operational Administrator to join a busy FMCG operation at our Boston site.

description:
BCP are part of Barrett Steel, the UK s largest steel distributor and processor, with over 160 years of heritage we are still family owned and operate from 29 sites across the UK and Ireland, holding more than 120,000 tonnes of steel stock. Although we are a business with significant scale, our success is built on the people who make it happen every day. We continually invest in our people, the latest processing machinery, technology, and materials-handling equipment so that we can deliver an exceptional service to our customers. Our people, our customers, and the communities in which we operate are at the heart of what we do. We are a forward-thinking business that values hard work, ambition, teamwork, and are always open to new ideas.

All about the role

To support the efficient operation of the production function by coordinating plans, processing orders, managing incoming loads and providing accurate administrative support across production, sales and logistics. The hours are Monday to Friday 8.30 am to 4.30 pm.

Key Responsibilities
- Prepare, maintain and update production plans and schedules in line with customer demand, available capacity and delivery requirements.
- Monitor production progress, identify potential delays and communicate priorities or changes to relevant teams.

- Process and manage intergroup sales orders, ensuring pricing, quantities, delivery dates and documentation are accurate.
- Release production orders within the relevant system in accordance with the agreed schedule and material availability.
- Check order information before release and resolve any missing or conflicting data with the appropriate department.
- Build and coordinate incoming loads, recording expected deliveries and ensuring load details are communicated to Warehouse and Production teams.
- Maintain accurate records for incoming materials, production orders, stock movements and delivery documentation.
- Carry out production programming, entering and maintaining job, machine or process instructions within company systems.
- Ensure programmes and production data reflect current specifications, priorities and required completion dates.
- Produce and distribute production paperwork, reports, schedules, labels and supporting documentation as required.
- Complete general administrative duties, including data entry, filing, document control, email correspondence and responding to internal queries.
- Maintain high standards of data accuracy and confidentiality across all systems and records.
- Support continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to simplify administrative processes and improve production efficiency.
- Comply with company procedures, health and safety requirements and quality standards at all times.
- Undertake other reasonable duties required to support the Production and Operations teams.

Skills and Attributes
- Strong organisational, planning and prioritisation skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Clear written and verbal communication skills.
- Confident working with multiple departments and managing changing priorities.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook.
- Ability to learn production planning and programming systems.
- Proactive, dependable and able to work independently as well as part of a team.
- Calm and methodical when working to deadlines in a busy manufacturing environment.

We offer you

- Pension & Life Assurance
- Discounts on retail and leisure
- Access to health and well being services

- Permanent position offering long-term stability within a growing organisation.
- Company pension scheme and holiday allowance.
- Training and development opportunities to build your skills.
- Employee assistance programme to support your wellbeing.
- Career progression opportunities as the business continues to grow.

Your responsibilities as Supply Chain Coordinator
- Raise and track purchase orders, ensuring materials arrive on time to meet production requirements.
- Monitor stock levels, support inventory planning and help prevent shortages or unnecessary delays.
- Liaise with suppliers on pricing, lead times and deliveries, resolving issues before they affect operations.
- Work closely with warehouse, production and logistics teams to keep goods moving efficiently.
- Maintain accurate records, monitor supplier performance and produce reports on stock availability and delivery performance.
- Support demand forecasting and identify opportunities to reduce costs, improve processes and strengthen service levels.

What we're looking for in a Supply Chain Coordinator
- Previous experience in supply chain, logistics, procurement or inventory management.
- Experience managing purchase orders, monitoring stock levels and communicating with suppliers.
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel, with the ability to maintain accurate records and analyse data.
- Experience using ERP, MRP or inventory management systems would be advantageous.
- Knowledge of stock planning, demand forecasting or import/export procedures would be beneficial.

If you enjoy keeping things organised, solving problems and making sure everything runs to plan, this could be the ideal next step. Apply today for this Supply Chain Coordinator position and put your experience to work in a business where your contribution will make a difference.

title: Trainee Legal Secretary
description:
Trainee Legal Secretary

Spalding

We are delighted to be working with a highly regarded national law firm on the appointment of a Trainee Float Team Legal Secretary to join their busy Spalding office.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to begin or develop their career within the legal sector, offering the chance to gain valuable experience across a variety of legal departments within an established and respected firm.

The Opportunity

If you enjoy variety, like staying busy and are keen to learn, this could be the perfect role for you.

As a Trainee Float Team Legal Secretary, you will spend time supporting different legal departments across the office, providing essential secretarial and administrative assistance to fee earners and wider teams. With exposure to different areas of law, no two days will be the same, giving you the opportunity to develop a broad skill set and gain an insight into how a busy legal practice operates.

You will play an important role in helping the teams run efficiently, ensuring that administrative tasks are completed accurately and that clients receive a professional and helpful service.

Key Responsibilities

Your duties will include:
- Providing secretarial and administrative support across a range of legal departments
- Preparing, formatting and amending correspondence and legal documents
- Managing incoming and outgoing communications, including telephone calls and emails
- Assisting with document management, filing and maintaining accurate records
- Supporting diary management, appointments and general departmental administration
- Helping to ensure client information and documentation are handled professionally and confidentially
- Working collaboratively with solicitors, fee earners and colleagues across the office
- Learning new processes and adapting to the requirements of different teams

About You

We are looking for an enthusiastic, organised and proactive individual who is keen to learn and enjoys working in a varied, fast-paced environment.

You will ideally have:
- Strong organisational skills and excellent attention to detail
- Good written and verbal communication skills
- A professional and friendly telephone manner
- Good IT skills and confidence using Microsoft Office
- The ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritise effectively
- A flexible approach and the willingness to support different teams as required
- A positive attitude, eagerness to learn and a genuine interest in developing a career within the legal sector
- The ability to work well both independently and as part of a team

Previous legal secretarial experience would be beneficial, but a willingness to learn, a positive attitude and a strong work ethic are equally important.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is a fantastic opportunity to gain hands-on experience within a professional legal environment while developing the skills and confidence needed to build a career in legal administration.

The float team structure offers exposure to multiple legal departments, allowing you to broaden your knowledge, learn from experienced professionals and discover different areas of the legal sector.

If you are looking for a role that offers variety, development and the opportunity to become a valued member of a busy team, this could be an excellent next step.

Interested?

If you are organised, enthusiastic and looking for an opportunity to start or develop your career as a Legal Secretary in Spalding, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now or contact us for a confidential discussion about the opportunity.

title: Patient Administrator
company: Lincolnshire Community Health Service NHS Trust
advertiser_name: Lincolnshire Community Health Service NHS Trust
description: Do you have excellent communication and administration skills with recent experience of working in a busy office environment where no two days are the same? Are you a proficient Microsoft Office and IT user? If you're looking for a rewarding administrative role where you can make a positive difference to people's experience of the NHS, then joining our patient admin services team and working alongside our community nursing and specialist services colleagues could be right for you. We're looking for experienced administrators who can transfer their skills to the NHS, ensuring that our community clinicians and patients are always supported with expert admin help. You should be willing and available to work on a rota basis usually between 0800-17:00hrs Monday to Friday. Roles in Lincoln/Skegness & Mablethorpe - other bases to be confirmed but can potentially work from any of our offices countywide Following policies, procedures and quality standards, to provide a professional and efficient administrative service which enables our clinical teams to focus on delivering patient care. To be the first person our patients see when they arrive at the health clinic and ensure a welcoming environment. To communicate in a timely, sensitive and empathetic manner with patients and clients either verbally or non-verbally, ensuring accurate details are recorded and either actioned or passed in a timely manner to the responsible person/team. To support our clinical teams to ensure they have enough stock, paperwork and equipment to complete their day to day tasks. Provide a range of administrative functions, which may include producing letters, processing patient referrals, scanning, photocopying, taking minutes, booking rooms, sorting post and other office/administration duties. Welcome our patient as they arrive at the reception desks of the health clinic and ensure their arrival is logged on our patient information system Monitor voicemails and respond to enquiries from patients and clients, including handling potentially difficult calls, in a professional manner, assessing the urgency, taking messages and passing to the relevant person where necessary. Book, amend or cancel patient appointments, by telephone or face to face, ensuring all records are updated and patients and clients are informed. Advise patients on access to and use of services. Maintain accurate patient records using both computer and paper. Receive, record, transmit, store and retrieve information from paper or electronic records and databases. Open and close the clinic Assist in the monitoring, control and ordering of stock and supplies in accordance with LCHS procedures. Unlock premises/ensure premises are securely locked and alarms are set prior to leaving the premises, if required. Adhere to LCHS's information governance requirements, treat all information as confidential and abide by the Data Protection Act.
